task.description: Independently validate TEST-DESIGNER's new regression test for ISS-0048 (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, describe 'owning process killed between claim/2 and release/2 (ISS-0048 regression)'). Do not trust TEST-DESIGNER's self-reported fail-then-pass output -- re-derive it yourself: run the current test suite on this branch and confirm it's green (mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs), and independently verify the test genuinely exercises a process-kill path (Process.exit(pid, :kill)) rather than a raised exception, since a raise-based test would prove nothing new (try/rescue already covered that before this fix). Also check: is the new describe/test name combined length safely under 200 chars (this project has hit ExUnit's 255-char SystemLimitError ceiling five times, see docs/anti-patterns.md); is the fixture self-sufficient/isolated (no cross-test state leakage); does test/specs/ISS-0048.md accurately describe the acceptance criterion.

result.summary: Independently re-validated TEST-DESIGNER's ISS-0048 regression test; all 5 acceptance criteria confirmed. (1) Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs --seed 0` myself on branch feature/WF03-ISS0048-20260818: '8 tests, 0 failures' -- matches TEST-DESIGNER's self-report, not taken on trust. (2) Read the new test (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:366-421) directly: it spawns an owner process via plain `spawn/1`, has it call `SandboxPool.claim/2`, then kills it with `Process.exit(owner_pid, :kill)` (line 401) confirmed via the test's own `Process.monitor/1` + `assert_receive {:DOWN, ..., :killed}` -- a genuine exit-signal kill, not a raised exception; grepped the file and found no `raise`/`try/rescue` construction around the kill path. Also independently diffed `lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` between merge-base bc7705d and current HEAD: bc7705d's `handle_info({:DOWN, ...})` only handles a *waiter* ref (nil branch is a no-op for an active-claim owner's ref), while the current version adds the `find_active_by_owner_ref/2` branch that drops the schema and frees the slot -- structurally confirms the pre-fix code genuinely could not have passed this test, corroborating TEST-DESIGNER's fail-then-pass claim beyond just re-reading its self-report. (3) Combined describe+test name measured directly: 170 chars (`wc -c` on the concatenated describe+test strings), under both the 200-char check and ExUnit's 255-char SystemLimitError ceiling. (4) Fixture isolation confirmed: each test calls `start_pool!/1` which starts a uniquely-named pool instance (`System.unique_integer/1`-suffixed) with its own `on_exit` `GenServer.stop`; the new test's schema is dropped via its own `on_exit(fn -> drop_schema!(schema_name) end)` plus the pool's own owner-crash reclaim; no shared mutable state referenced across tests; the new test does not depend on any other test having run. (5) Grepped for hardcoded secrets/connection strings in both files -- none found (DB access goes through `Letflow.Repo`/`DataCase`, no literal credentials). (6) test/specs/ISS-0048.md checked line-by-line against the actual test code -- assertion order, helper names (`wait_until_schema_dropped/2`), spawn-not-Task rationale, and the fail-then-pass commit SHAs (bc7705d pre-fix, ef1e4c8/729e7b4 post-fix) all accurately reflect the code as it exists on this branch.
